Scaling and Partitioning

TaktX is designed for horizontal scalability. Both topics and state stores are partitioned, allowing the system to handle increasing workloads by adding more engine nodes and partitions.

Partitioning Strategy

Kafka’s partitioning ensures that related messages (e.g., for a specific process instance) are routed to the same partition, maintaining consistency and enabling parallel processing. However, it is important to note that Kafka only allows partition counts to be increased—not decreased—after topic creation. Increasing the number of partitions can have a significant impact on processing, as it may cause rebalancing and redistribution of data and workload across engine nodes.

Because of this, we currently recommend only increasing partition counts when no engine nodes are running. This avoids potential inconsistencies, processing interruptions, or unexpected behavior during rebalancing.

Initial Scaling Recommendations

For initial deployments, we recommend a partition-to-thread (CPU core) ratio of 1:1 to 1.5. For example, if you plan to assign 4 to 6 CPU cores or threads to your engine nodes, start with 4 partitions. This ensures efficient resource utilization and balanced workload distribution across engine nodes.

Performance Benchmarking

For more detailed guidance on sizing and scaling, as well as real-world performance data, please refer to the TaktX performance benchmark documentation

Best Practices

Monitor partition distribution and consumer lag to ensure optimal performance. Adjust partition counts and node capacity as needed, but always plan partition increases during maintenance windows when no engine nodes are running.
